Η νέα προσφορά συνδυάζει αποθήκευση ενέργειας μπαταρίας, επιλογές χρηματοδότησης και εμπορία ηλεκτρικής ενέργειας για να βοηθήσει τα εργοστάσια να βελτιστοποιήσουν την κατανάλωση ενέργειας, κόκκινο…
items.descriptionOriginal: Saft, a global leader in advanced battery technology and a wholly owned subsidiary of TotalEnergies, has launched EnerShift, an integrated energy solution designed for energy-intensive industrial facilities. The new offering combines battery energy storage, financing options and electricity trading to help factories optimize energy consumption, reduce electricity bills and improve financial returns. EnerShift enables industrial operators to finance, deploy and optimize battery energy storage systems (BESS) while generating additional revenue through participation in electricity markets. The integrated solution addresses key financial and operational challenges faced by manufacturers seeking more flexible, affordable and sustainable energy systems. The offering builds on Saft’s expertise in advanced battery technologies, energy management, financing solutions and electricity market optimization. The company can support customers throughout the entire project lifecycle, from initial feasibility studies and business case assessments to financing, equipment installation and long-term operational management. One of EnerShift’s major advantages is its ability to generate additional economic value from battery storage through electricity market participation. By intelligently managing battery charging and discharging according to market conditions, industrial facilities can optimize electricity purchases, benefit from price fluctuations and maximize the value of their energy flexibility. This allows businesses to generate additional revenue without increasing the operational workload of their on-site teams. “Many industrial companies understand the operational benefits of energy storage, but financing and profitability often remain barriers to investment. Our objective is to help customers not only deploy battery systems but also maximize their economic return throughout the asset’s lifetime”, said Vincent Le Quintrec, ESS Sales Director at Saft. Saft’s Bordeaux project showcases EnerShift’s benefits Saft is demonstrating the EnerShift model through an industrial-scale energy storage project at its Bordeaux production facility in France. The installation combines a 9 MWh battery energy storage system with advanced energy management software and electricity trading capabilities. By optimizing electricity consumption and adjusting battery charging and discharging schedules according to market conditions, the Bordeaux facility is targeting approximately 15% annual savings on its electricity costs. Including additional financial benefits generated through electricity market participation, the project is expected to achieve a payback period of approximately five years. Beyond reducing energy expenses, the installation is designed to strengthen the facility’s operational resilience and support Saft’s broader decarbonization objectives. The project demonstrates how battery storage can improve industrial energy efficiency while creating additional economic opportunities. EnerShift boosts industrial competitiveness Beyond lowering electricity bills, the multiple revenue streams generated by battery storage can improve investment returns and shorten payback periods for industrial operators. These systems can become strategic assets that enhance energy security, improve operational reliability, accelerate the transition toward cleaner energy and create lasting competitive advantages. By combining advanced battery technology, financing solutions and energy market optimization, Saft aims to make industrial energy storage more accessible and financially attractive. EnerShift also highlights the growing importance of energy flexibility in helping manufacturers manage electricity price fluctuations, improve productivity and achieve their sustainability targets.

items.descriptionOriginal: Ο πρόεδρος της Ουκρανίας, Βολοντίμιρ Ζελένσκι ζήτησε σήμερα από τη Μαδρίτη τη βοήθεια της Ισπανίας και χωρών της Λατινικής Αμερικής για την «ανοικοδόμηση και την αποκατάσταση του ενεργειακού συστήματος» της χώρας του, το οποίο έχει καταστραφεί από τις ρωσικές επιθέσεις. «Έχουμε ανάγκη όσο το δυνατόν μεγαλύτερη διεθνή συνεργασία προκειμένου να συνεχίσουμε να ανοικοδομούμε και να αποκαθιστάμε το ενεργειακό μας σύστημα, κάτι που έχουμε επειγόντως ανάγκη», είπε ο Ουκρανός ηγέτης κατά τη διάρκεια μιας συνάντησης στο περιθώριο της 30ης Ιβηρο-αμερικανικής Συνόδου, η οποία ολοκληρώθηκε σήμερα στην ισπανική πρωτεύουσα. «Χρειαζόμαστε υλικά, περισσότερα υλικά: μετασχηματιστές, ηλεκτρικά καλώδια, σύγχρονο ηλεκτρονικό εξοπλισμό, καθώς και διάφορους τύπους γεννητριών, τόσο πετρελαίου όσο και φυσικού αερίου», περιέγραψε ο Βολοντίμιρ Ζελένσκι παρουσία μεταξύ άλλων του Ισπανού πρωθυπουργού Πέδρο Σάντσεθ , των προέδρων της Γουατεμάλας και της Ονδούρας, Μπερνάρδο Αρέβαλο και Νάσρι Ασφούρα , καθώς και του γενικού γραμματέα του Οργανισμού Ηνωμένων Εθνών, Αντόνιο Γκουτέρες και του προέδρου του Ευρωπαϊκού Συμβουλίου, Αντόνιο Κόστα. «Γνωρίζουμε πως εταιρείες στην Ισπανία και τη Λατινική Αμερική μπορούν να μας βοηθήσουν σε αυτήν την προσπάθεια», συνέχισε ο ίδιος, κάνοντας αναφορά σε «μετασχηματιστές που προέρχονται από τη Βραζιλία, το Μεξικό, την Αργεντινή και την Κολομβία», «ηλεκτρικά καλώδια από τη Χιλή» ή «ηλεκτρονικούς εξοπλισμούς, καλώδια και γεννήτριες που κατασκευάζονται στην Ισπανία». «Είναι τόσο σημαντικό», υπογράμμισε: «Χρειαζόμαστε εξοπλισμό συμβατό με το δίκτυό μας ηλεκτρικής ενέργειας και τον χρειαζόμαστε γρήγορα. Παρακαλούμε, λοιπόν, να μας παρέχετε άμεση υποστήριξη διευκολύνοντας την επικοινωνία με τις εταιρείες και τις παραγωγικές σας δυνατότητες, ώστε αυτές οι προμήθειες να φτάσουν στην Ουκρανία το συντομότερο δυνατό». Η επίσκεψη στην Ισπανία του επικεφαλής του ουκρανικού κράτους, ο οποίος την Τρίτη βρισκόταν στο Βερολίνο, διεξήχθη με φόντο τις νέες διπλωματικές προσπάθειες με στόχο την αναζωογόνηση των ελπίδων για ειρήνη και της πρόσφατης προσέγγισης μεταξύ Ντόναλντ Τραμπ και Βλαντίμιρ Πούτιν. Αυτές οι προσπάθειες έχουν προκαλέσει φόβους στο Κίεβο για μια πιθανή αμερικανική απόσυρση της υποστήριξης, σε μια εποχή που η Ουκρανία προετοιμάζεται για έναν δύσκολο χειμώνα ενόψει των έντονων ρωσικών βομβαρδισμών. Περισσότερα από τεσσεράμισι χρόνια μετά την έναρξη της ρωσικής εισβολής, οι διαπραγματεύσεις μεταξύ Κιέβου, Μόσχας και Ουάσινγκτον έχουν προγραμματιστεί να επαναληφθούν στις 10 και 11 Νοεμβρίου στα Ηνωμένα Αραβικά Εμιράτα, υπό αμερικανική μεσολάβηση. Σε συνέντευξή του στον γερμανικό δημόσιο ραδιοτηλεοπτικό φορέα ZDF , ο Ουκρανός πρόεδρος δήλωσε ότι η νίκη των Δημοκρατικών στις ενδιάμεσες εκλογές των ΗΠΑ τροφοδότησε την «ελπίδα» για αυξημένη υποστήριξη από την Ουάσινγκτον προς το Κίεβο. Πηγή: ΑΠΕ-ΜΠΕ www.ertnews.gr

items.title: Σχεδόν 50 χρόνια μετά την εκτόξευση, το Voyager 1 της NASA πλησιάζει ένα ιστορικό διαστημικό ορόσημο
items.titleOriginal: Nearly 50 years after launch, NASA’s Voyager 1 approaches a historic space milestone
items.description: Ο ανιχνευτής Voyager 1 της NASA, που εκτοξεύτηκε το 1977 για να εξερευνήσει τις εξωτερικές περιοχές του ηλιακού μας συστήματος, πρόκειται να φτάσει μια ημέρα φωτός μακριά από τον πλανήτη μας. Αρχικά ξεκίνησε για να μελετήσει τον Κρόνο και τον Δία για τριάντα μήνες, αλλά τον Αύγουστο του 2012, πέρασε από την άκρη του ηλιακού μας συστήματος, γνωστή ως ηλιόσφαιρα. Αυτή τη στιγμή είναι ο πιο απομακρυσμένος άνθρωπος…
items.descriptionOriginal: NASA’s Voyager 1 probe, launched back in 1977 to explore the outer reaches of our solar system, is due to reach one light day away from our planet. It originally set off to study Saturn and Jupiter for thirty months but during August 2012, it passed through the edge of our solar system known as the heliosphere. It is currently the furthest human-made object in our universe. As Voyager 1 traveled towards Jupiter on March 5th 1979, it discovered the ring that surrounds the planet as well as two new Jovian moons that had never been seen before Metis and Thebe. It also took pictures of Jupiter’s clouds and four of Jupiter’s main moons: Callisto, Ganymede, Europa, and Io. The closest approach to Saturn happened on November 12th 1980. Five new moons were found as well as a new ring that had not been spotted before. This ring, called the G-ring, contains lots of small moons that help to keep the rings in orbit. Nearly 50 years of space discoveries Researchers studied the atmosphere of the moon Titan and found it to be made up largely of nitrogen (about 90%) with some hydrocarbons and methane. This could mean that it would be able to help start the development of pre-biotic chemistry. On January 1st 1990, the Voyager Interstellar Mission began as the probe traveled further through our solar system. On February 26th 1998, Voyager 1 became the farthest human-made object in space after surpassing Pioneer 10. On August 25th 2012, Voyager 1 passed through the heliosphere to study the interstellar medium. The probe took the famous Pale Blue Dot picture of our planet from 40 AU away. Despite travelling for fifty years, NASA is still receiving signals from the probe. However, with less power left, NASA has been turning off equipment. Recently another piece of equipment was turned off to ensure that data can continue to be sent back. There are only four pieces of scientific equipment left on board Voyager 1. These are the magnetometer, plasma wave’s instrument, and cosmic ray telescope and low energy charged particle instrument. The probe is powered by three RTGs (radioisotope thermoelectric generators). They use the heat produced by the decay of plutonium-238 to create electricity. The probe also contains a 30cm gold-plated copper record known as the “Golden Record”. This contains 115 pictures of life on earth , 90 minutes of music, greetings in 55 languages and sounds from earth. It also contains messages from former UN Secretary-General Kurt Waldheim and former American President Jimmy Carter. The probe is almost one light day away meaning that any radio waves or light between Earth and the probe will take 24 hours to reach each other. The journey that Voyager 1 has undertaken is amazing and has given researchers valuable information about what lies outside our solar system.

items.title: Το ηλεκτρόδιο που μοιάζει με στόκο θα μπορούσε να βελτιώσει τη φωνητική αποκατάσταση
items.titleOriginal: Putty-like electrode could improve vocal rehabilitation
items.description: Μια ομάδα ερευνητών του Πανεπιστημίου McGill ανέπτυξε ένα ηλεκτρόδιο που μοιάζει με στόκο που διαμορφώνεται στο δέρμα για να βελτιώσει τη θεραπεία και την παρακολούθηση των διαταραχών της φωνής και των ασθενειών των ανώτερων αεραγωγών. Σε μια μελέτη απόδειξης της ιδέας, ο αισθητήρας ταίριαξε με ένα τυπικό κλινικό ηλεκτρόδιο για θόρυβο και σταθερότητα ενώ καταγράφει δραστηριότητα από μικρούς μύες του λαιμού.
items.descriptionOriginal: A team of McGill University researchers has developed a putty-like electrode that molds to the skin to improve treatment and monitoring of voice disorders and upper airway diseases. In a proof-of-concept study, the sensor matched a standard clinical electrode for noise and stability while recording activity from small neck muscles.

items.descriptionOriginal: Vitamin B12 is essential for the body's proper functioning and is found in foods of animal origin. It is produced by certain bacteria that, in addition to being found in nature, are cultivated at industrial facilities for commercial use, primarily by the food and pharmaceutical industries. It is beneficial when certain nutritional deficiencies are present, and in recent times it has become popular, along with other B vitamins, as a remedy for hangovers, as it can help reduce fatigue.

items.descriptionOriginal: X-ray experiments at Brookhaven National Laboratory have begun to steer themselves. Machine learning picks which parts of a sample to examine in detail, rebuilds 3D images as data arrive and, in one test, did the job with nearly one tenth of the usual data. The demonstrations at the National Synchrotron Light Source II (NSLS-II), a U.S. Department of Energy user facility, are early results from SYNAPS-I, short for Synergistic Neutron and Photon Science – Intelligence. It is a seed project under the ModCon initiative in the DOE’s Genesis Mission, led by Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory’s Advanced Light Source with Argonne, Oak Ridge, SLAC and Brookhaven. The collaboration combines open-source models, industry partnerships and advanced computing resources. Letting the data pick the target At NSLS-II’s Hard X-ray Nanoprobe, an X-ray microscope for 2D and 3D nanoscale imaging, a team led by lead beamline scientist Hanfei Yan ran an automated experiment that analyzed images as they were acquired. It flagged scientifically interesting regions of a complex sample and picked those spots for follow-up high-resolution scans, with no human intervention. “This enables an automated experiment to run for hours, surveying a large area, and collect high-fidelity data only from scientifically important locations,” said Daniel Allan, who leads NSLS-II’s Data Engineering Group. Conventional methods can’t do this reliably, he said. A microchip in 3D, in real time A second test focused on ptychographic tomography, a computational technique that builds detailed 3D images from many individual measurements, using microelectronic chips as samples. A foundation model trained at Argonne replaced the slow iterative process normally used to reconstruct the images. Working with NVIDIA and its Holoscan platform, the team reconstructed images in real time at 200 images per second. A model developed and trained at NSLS-II reconstructed a microchip from nearly one-tenth of the data normally required, which helps with thin, flat samples where complete tomographic datasets are hard to collect. The team then fine-tuned Meta’s open-weight Segment Anything Model 3 for chip imaging so it could automatically pick out materials, structures and regions of interest in the 3D volume. Together, the steps can cut scan time and radiation dose while speeding up interpretation. Why it matters beyond chips Yan said the technique could help any field that needs fast, high-resolution X-ray tomography and rapid 3D data analysis. Examples include finding buried structures and defects in microelectronics, studying degradation in battery electrodes and characterizing complex nanomaterials. The tools also help users make better use of limited beam time, he said. Tomography while the experiment runs The team plans to train more robust foundation models on more diverse datasets and extend the approach to other 3D imaging techniques . A key goal is real-time tomography. Today, researchers usually collect an entire projection dataset before reconstructing it. In a real-time workflow, reconstruction would start during the experiment, with a low-resolution image sharpening as more measurements arrive. Paired with automated feature detection, that would let beamlines adapt on their own to what they see. Sean McSweeney, NSLS-II’s interim deputy for strategy, said such workflows will be integral to next-generation user facilities. Alexander Hexemer, the SYNAPS-I lead contact at the Advanced Light Source, said facilities share the same challenges, from data volumes that outpace human analysis to reconstruction bottlenecks, and that no one facility can solve them alone. As these technologies mature, the goal is not simply to process experimental data faster. It is to tighten the link between measurement, analysis, and scientific decision-making, so experiments can respond to what they discover as they run.

items.descriptionOriginal: For decades, people using 3D printers have faced a tough decision: print quickly, print parts with fine features or print materials that meet performance requirements. Light-based 3D printers are fast and precise but limited in what materials they can use. Extrusion-based techniques can handle a wider range of functional materials but sacrifice speed and fine details.

items.descriptionOriginal: Όσο πιο καθυστερημένο, τόσο πιο δύσκολο. Μπορεί ο Ρονάλντο να ήταν ένας αρνητής της ήττας, αλλά όσο κι αν το πάλευε, δεν θα μπορούσε να νικήσει το αναπόφευκτο. Και εξαιτίας αυτής της επιμονής του, «ξόδεψε» πολύ από τον μύθο που είχε χτίσει ο ίδιος για τον εαυτό του. Ο καθυστερημένος αποχαιρετισμός του τον έκανε όλο και πιο γήινο στα μάτια των ποδοσφαιρόφιλων. Έτσι, έπειτα από ένα άγονο Μουντιάλ στο οποίο έκανε «θόρυβο» μόνο για λάθος λόγους και ακόμα ακόμη καβγά με ομοσπονδιακό προπονητή, ο Ρονάλντο ανακοίνωσε στα 41 του, το τέλος μιας διεθνούς διαδρομής που ξεκίνησε το 2003 και περιέλαβε έξι Μουντιάλ και ένα Ευρωπαϊκό τρόπαιο. Σε αυτήν τη διαδρομή υπάρχουν στιγμές χαράς, υπάρχουν και εκείνες της ντροπής. Όσο πιο έντονη η προσωπικότητα, τόσο πιο δυνατό είναι το συναίσθημα. Αυτή η αρχή της αναλογικότητας είχε διαταραχτεί τα τελευταία χρόνια: η επιμονή του να παραμένει στο επίκεντρο έκανε τη συζήτηση να περιστρέφεται γύρω από εκείνον και όχι γύρω από την εθνική ομάδα. Κάποτε αυτό μπορεί να ήταν το μεγαλύτερο πλεονέκτημα της Πορτογαλίας. Στα τελευταία χρόνια κατέληξε να είναι το δυσεπίλυτο πρόβλημά της. Ρονάλντο: Οι τρεις πιο ντροπιαστικές στιγμές 1. Ο αρχηγός που εγκατέλειψε την αποστολή Είναι 30 Σεπτεμβρίου 2026 όταν ο Ρονάλντο αποχωρεί χωρίς άδεια και φεύγει από την Κοπεγχάγη, πριν από τον αγώνα της Πορτογαλίας με τη Δανία. Αιτία: Η μη χρησιμοποίησή του από τον Ζόρζε Ζέσους, παρόλο που σηκώθηκε για ζέσταμα. Φυσικά και υπό άλλες συνθήκες ο Ζέσους θα έπρεπε να ήταν ήδη σε αναζήτηση νέας ομάδας. Διαβάστε ακόμα Όμως η Ομοσπονδία αποφάσισε να σκεφτεί ποδοσφαιρικά. Τιμώρησε τον Ρονάλντο, τον αρχηγό της ομάδας και σύμβολο ενός ολόκληρου λαού, για αυτή του τη συμπεριφορά. Ένας αρχηγός είναι ο ηγέτης στο γήπεδο, στα αποδυτήρια, στο ξενοδοχείο όπου καταλύει η ομάδα, ακόμη και στο λεωφορείο. Ο Ρονάλντο είχε για άλλη μια φορά σκεφτεί παρορμητικά, βάζοντας τον εγωισμό του πιο πάνω από την ομάδα και τους συμπαίκτες του. Δεν ήταν η πρώτη φορά. Θα ήταν όμως η τελευταία. 2. Άλλοι πανηγυρίζουν, άλλος διαμαρτύρεται Υπάρχουν στιγμές που μπορεί να περιγράφουν μια ολόκληρη καριέρα. Όπως για παράδειγμα εκείνη στο Μουντιάλ του 2022, όταν ο Μπρούνο Φερνάντες σκοράρει εναντίον των Ουρουγουανών. Όλοι οι Πορτογάλοι πανηγυρίζουν εκτός από έναν, τον αρχηγό! Ο Ρονάλντο τρέχει πίσω από τον διαιτητή όταν συνειδητοποιεί πως το γκολ έχει πιστωθεί στον συμπαίκτη του και όχι στον ίδιο. Για την ακρίβεια, ο Μπρούνο Φερνάντες σεντράρει, ο Ρονάλντο προσπαθεί να πάρει την κεφαλιά και η μπάλα έπειτα από τρεις στιγμές αναπαύεται στα δίχτυα. Όμως το τσιπάκι στην μπάλα επιβεβαίωσε ότι δεν υπήρξε επαφή με το κεφάλι του. Η επιμονή για την πατρότητα του γκολ ήταν εκείνη που έκανε την ιστορία τόσο άβολη. Για έναν ποδοσφαιριστή του μεγέθους και των γκολ που έχει σημειώσει, ήταν ένα εντυπωσιακό δείγμα μικροψυχίας. 3. Η ρήξη με τον Φερνάντο Σάντος Στις 6 Δεκεμβρίου 2022 ο τότε προπονητής της Πορτογαλίας, Φερνάντο Σάντος, κάνει την επανάστασή του, η οποία «θα πνιγεί στο ίδιο του το αίμα». Η απόφασή του να αφήσει τον Ρονάλντο στον πάγκο εναντίον της Ελβετίας, στη φάση των 16 του Μουντιάλ του Κατάρ, ήταν η απαρχή μιας κόντρας που έφερε αργότερα την απόλυση του τεχνικού. Έναν χρόνο αργότερα, τον Νοέμβριο του 2023, ο προπονητής αποκάλυψε ότι εκείνος και ο Ρονάλντο δεν είχαν μιλήσει έπειτα από την επιστροφή τους από το Μουντιάλ. Περιέγραψε μια σχέση σχεδόν πατέρα και γιου και εξήγησε ότι ο Ρονάλντο είχε παρερμηνεύσει την απόφασή του. Ο ίδιος επέμενε ότι θα έκανε ξανά την ίδια επιλογή για το καλό της ομάδας. Διαβάστε ακόμα Δεν έχει τεκμηριωθεί ότι ο Ρονάλντο προκάλεσε την απομάκρυνση του Σάντος. Η επίσημη εκδοχή ήταν η κοινή συμφωνία για την έναρξη νέου κύκλου, μετά τον αποκλεισμό από το Μαρόκο. Η προσωπική ρήξη, ωστόσο, σημαίνει πολλά παραπάνω για τα δύο μέρη: Κάποτε, ήταν οι δυο τους που πιστώνονταν πρώτοι την κατάκτηση του Euro 2016. Όλα ήταν καλά, μέχρι που ο Σάντος έκρινε πως ο Κριστιάνο θα πρέπει να καθίσει στον πάγκο. Οι τρεις θριαμβευτικές στιγμές 1. Η βραδιά που νίκησε τον Ιμπραΐμοβιτς και έστειλε την Πορτογαλία στο Μουντιάλ Στις 19 Νοεμβρίου 2013, στη Σουηδία, ο Ρονάλντο έδωσε ίσως την καθαρότερη απάντηση στο γιατί μια ολόκληρη χώρα είχε μάθει να περιμένει από εκείνον τη λύση. Στη ρεβάνς των μπαράζ για το Μουντιάλ, ο πολύς Ζλάταν Ιμπραΐμοβιτς πέτυχε δύο γκολ. Η απάντηση είχε την υπογραφή του μεγάλου αντιπάλου του: Ο Κριστιάνο πέτυχε τρία, η Πορτογαλία νίκησε 3-2 και πήρε την πρόκριση. Εκείνη τη βραδιά δύο τεράστια «Εγώ» του παγκοσμίου ποδοσφαίρου συγκρούστηκαν. Ο Ρονάλντο δεν είχε κανένα θέμα να δείξει πως το δικό του ήταν το μεγαλύτερο! 2. Το χατ τρικ απέναντι στην Ισπανία Στις 15 Ιουνίου 2018, στην πρεμιέρα του Μουντιάλ, πέτυχε και τα τρία γκολ της Πορτογαλίας στο 3-3 με την Ισπανία. Το τελευταίο ήρθε με απευθείας φάουλ στο 88ο λεπτό, όταν η ομάδα του βρισκόταν πίσω στο σκορ. Ήταν μια εμφάνιση που χωρούσε όλα όσα τον έκαναν σπουδαίο: τεχνική, αποφασιστικότητα και την πεποίθηση ότι υπήρχε ακόμη χρόνος να αλλάξει το αποτέλεσμα. Η Ισπανία είχε περισσότερες λύσεις. Η Πορτογαλία είχε CR7 . 3. Ακόμα ένας τίτλος στα 40 Αν κάτι λειτούργησε αποτρεπτικά σε μια… πρώιμη συνταξιοδότηση του Ρονάλντο, αυτό ήταν η κατάκτηση του Nations League του 2025. Ο «μπομπέρ» βρήκε ένα νέο αφήγημα, αφού η ηλικία… «είναι απλά ένας αριθμός». Σκόραρε το νικητήριο γκολ στον ημιτελικό απέναντι στη Γερμανία και ισοφάρισε την Ισπανία στον τελικό, πριν η Πορτογαλία κατακτήσει το τρόπαιο στα πέναλτι. Αυτή η επιτυχία εξηγεί και γιατί το αντίο ήταν τόσο δύσκολο. Όποτε η συζήτηση έφτανε στο τέλος, εκείνος μπορούσε ακόμη να εμφανιστεί με ένα γκολ που την ανέβαλλε. Κάπως έτσι, αποχώρησε από την ενεργό δράση με τις μεγάλες βραδιές να είναι χρόνια πίσω του, σε αντίθεση με τον Μέσι, που αποχώρησε έπειτα από ένα τελικό Μουντιάλ. Η κορυφαία στιγμή της Πορτογαλίας: Το Euro 2016 Στις 10 Ιουλίου 2016, η Πορτογαλία κατέκτησε το πρώτο μεγάλο τρόπαιο της ιστορίας της, νικώντας τη Γαλλία με 1-0 στην παράταση. Όμως, ο Ρονάλντο τραυματίστηκε και αποχώρησε νωρίς. Το γκολ του τίτλου πέτυχε ο one – hit wonder Έντερ, με τον Ρονάλντο να δίνει το δικό του σόου, όρθιος δίπλα στον Φερνάντο Σάντος. Η κορυφαία στιγμή της χώρας του περιείχε μια αλήθεια που ο ίδιος δυσκολεύτηκε αργότερα να αποδεχθεί: η Πορτογαλία μπορούσε να τα καταφέρει και χωρίς εκείνον μέσα στο γήπεδο. Αυτό δεν μειώνει τη συμβολή του στην κατάκτηση. Δίνει στην επιτυχία το πραγματικό της μέγεθος. Ο αρχηγός που είχε βοηθήσει την ομάδα να φτάσει μέχρι εκεί χρειάστηκε τους συμπαίκτες του για να ολοκληρώσουν τη διαδρομή. Κι εκείνοι το έκαναν. Αυτός είναι άλλωστε και ο ορισμός της ομάδας. Άσχετα αν ο ίδιος ο Ρονάλντο έβαζε τον εαυτό του πολλές φορές πάνω και από αυτήν! items.descriptionOriginal: T he staff at Erik’s Ranch & Retreats has a saying: Sheets, towels and lives changed daily . Erik’s Ranch is a guest retreat where autistic people are concierges, guides, wranglers, cooks and more. Located on 230 acres of pristine pasture and wilderness near Livingston, Montana, the ranch is less than an hour from Yellowstone National Park. It offers horseback riding, fly fishing, nature hikes, history walks and experiences with ranch animals and wildlife — most led or assisted by paid neurodivergent “members,” most of whom also live on the property. The inspiration for Erik’s Ranch dates back to 2008, when founder Kathryn Nordberg was pondering how her son, Erik, whom she described as “a moderately functioning teenager with autism,” would live as an adult — and particularly what would happen when she was no longer around. Ranch manager Cameron Porter (in black hat) and member John Rekedal help a visitor from New Jersey mount her steed for a trail ride. Credit: Jodi Hausen “As someone challenged with expressive language, there weren’t very many opportunities for kids like him,” she said, sitting in the well-appointed kitchen of the ranch’s six-bedroom lodge. So she established a nonprofit with a boutique-style hotel in Edina, Minnesota, where, even after she’s gone, Erik and others like him can live, work and thrive. There, adults on the autism spectrum work and live independently and are guided by life coaches toward achieving personal goals like interviewing, equine or cooking skills; or setting up an Etsy page to sell their artwork. Weighed down by negative news? Enter your email below to receive our smart, uplifting newsletters. Or click here to choose exactly which ones you want [contact-form-7] Using a similar model, in 2014 Nordberg opened the Montana ranch, where not only employees on the spectrum benefit: She designed most of the cabins specifically for neurodivergent guests. Though anyone can appreciate the soothing atmosphere, it’s particularly accommodating for those on the spectrum, who sometimes experience sensory overload. The calmingly simple cabins provide awe-inspiring vistas of the surrounding mountains with little to no sign of human activity. Hardware was selected to close drawers, cabinets and doors with hardly a sound. Walls, furnishings and bedding are muted earth tones and lights have dimmers. Credit: Jodi Hausen Erik’s Ranch is run primarily by young autistic people, some of whom also live on the property. The ranch has unparalleled views of the Absaroka-Beartooth Mountains. Autistic and other neurodivergent people are often misunderstood and feel out-of-place, experiencing discrimination, social exclusion, bullying and other situations that can lead to low self-esteem. That — and an inexorable need to mask their differences — often results in depression and anxiety. Some studies indicate that people on the spectrum are four times more likely to experience major depression compared with the general population. “Depression, loneliness, lack of confidence, feeling isolated, rejected, and a lack of community and people who care is what Erik’s Ranch is working to minimize and eliminate,” Nordberg said. And it’s working. John Rekedal, 21, lives in Minnesota but just spent his first summer working at the Montana ranch. When he’s home, he works in a large production greenhouse. And though his coworkers there are understanding, he prefers the camaraderie of working with the ranch’s small staff amid the hush of the surrounding mountains. Jacob Thoresen fetches horses from a pasture in preparation for a trail ride. Thoresen has been working for Erik’s Ranch and Retreats for 10 years. Credit: Jodi Hausen “I’m a whole lot more inclined to work outside,” he said. “And I know everyone’s name. It’s more relaxed.” Cornell University autism researcher Leslie Shaw analyzed a national sample of autistic adults who could answer a survey unassisted and found that only about 53 percent were working in 2023. Furthermore, in 2024, people with cognitive disabilities (of which neurodivergence is a subset) were employed at less than half the rate of people without any disability, according to Cornell’s Northeast ADA Center . These low employment rates may be due to neurotypical employers’ lack of experience with and understanding of neurodivergent people leading to misaligned work assignments, confusion and a fraught or untenable work environment. On a recent late summer day in Montana, Jacob Thoresen, 33, was gearing up to lead a small group of guests on a trail ride. He has been working with the nonprofit for 10 years and splits his time between its two locations. In black cowboy hat and jeans, he walked back and forth across the dirt-floored indoor arena to a tack room, gathering saddles and bridles. He saddled horses while other members dutifully scooped and cleaned areas around the animals. Credit: Jodi Hausen Erik’s Ranch & Retreats is part of a growing trend of workplaces designed to integrate people with autism or other disabilities. Thoresen had other jobs before coming to Erik’s. He was a baggage handler at the Minneapolis-Saint Paul Airport and worked in retail and manufacturing. He even tried a desk job. “But,” he said with a smile, “that isn’t me.” Thoresen said he’s gained confidence working with Erik’s Ranch & Retreats. “If you would have met me 10 years ago, I would have been, like, I couldn’t be able to do anything independent and be trusted to actually get the work done,” he said. “This place is teaching me how to be independent. In this last year, I’ve grown more.” He still gets support, but staff, recognizing his achievements, have loosened the reins. “I’m having to rely more on myself to work on those independent skills,” he added. Hannah Jacobs (left) helps Zoe Markman put fresh linens on a bed in one of the guest cabins at Erik’s Ranch. Credit: Jodi Hausen When asked what he finds challenging about working at Erik’s Ranch, Thoresen said workdays can be inconsistent. At the Minnesota retreat, he completes the same tasks daily. On the ranch, daily schedules shift and sometimes he gets overwhelmed. “But I can move through it,” he said. “I attribute that to the staff that I work with and just practice. They do a good job of seeing [my overwhelm] and being like, okay. And that helps, you know. I’ve had too many employers in the past that have been like, ‘Oh, you’re not having a good day? Well, just go home.’” Over the years, Erik’s Ranch & Retreats has employed 27 autistic young adults — 19 in the last year. The goal, Nordberg said, is to serve 30 members regularly. The organization is part of a growing trend of workplaces designed to integrate people with autism or other disabilities. John Rekedal helps clean around the horses in the indoor arena before a trail ride. Credit: Jodi Hausen Not far from Erik’s Ranch, Special K Ranch in Columbus, Montana, provides living quarters and jobs in farming, ranching and gardening and contracts with area businesses to employ adults with developmental disabilities. Over in Jackson, Wyoming, Vertical Harvest integrates people with a wide array of disabilities into their operations growing lettuces, microgreens, tomatoes and basil. In a fully accessible greenhouse, Vertical Harvest operates on what’s known as the “Grow Well” model of employment : providing opportunities for workers to pursue passions by creating or placing them in positions that correspond to their strengths and aspirations, their likes and dislikes. In other words, adapting the workplace to the employee rather than the other way around. Although she hadn’t heard of Grow Well, Nordberg embraces its philosophy. It doesn’t always work out as planned, though. “Not everyone wants to learn hospitality,” she said. In fact, one autistic young man told her he wanted to be a “white hat hacker,” using his computer skills for good. But she didn’t have a role that fit his skills and aspirations. In other instances, however, a member’s passions can be integrated into ranch operations. Part-time member Zoe Markman shows off a colorful collection of eggs gathered from the hens in the coop behind her. Credit: Jodi Hausen Zoe Markman, a 21-year-old autistic woman from Bozeman, loves animals — particularly chickens. So when Markman started working part-time at the ranch, Nordberg built a chicken coop and populated it with more than a dozen hens whom Markman gave punny names: Chiquille O’Neal, Princess Layer and Hen Solo. On a recent workday, Markman gathered more than a dozen colorful eggs. Nordberg also helped Erik start a baking business making cookies, brownies, scones and banana bread. Erik is a visual learner and communicator, so Nordberg created a pictorial cookbook with step-by-step instructions. She marked bins of flour, sugar and other ingredients with pictures so Erik can do most of the work independently. Wait, you're not a member yet? Join the Reasons to be Cheerful community by supporting our nonprofit publication and giving what you can. Join Cancel anytime The ranch can currently house five members and has five cabins and the lodge for guests on its expansive property. So Nordberg has room to expand, and she’d like to. But finances and land-use regulations present barriers. It’s expensive running a guest ranch, though the costs are partly covered by guest fees and philanthropy. And area permitting will only allow for seven more cabins. “This will never be a huge operation,” Nordberg said. But she’s gratified knowing there are places for Erik and others like him to live, belong and find meaningful work. This story was supported in part by the Solutions Journalism Network’s HEAL Fellowship. items.description: Ενώ οι millennials και οι Gen Zers συχνά συγκεντρώνονται ως η «νεανική ομάδα», σίγουρα δεν είναι το ίδιο. (Αν και είναι κάπως δύσκολο να το ξεχωρίσεις με όλη τη μόδα του Y2K που επιπλέει.) Αλλά μιλώντας ως millennial, σίγουρα έχουμε διαφορετικές προσεγγίσεις στη ζωή, πολλές από τις οποίες φαίνεται να καταλήγουν σε μια αίσθηση αυτοπεποίθησης. Αυτό ισχύει για το s…
items.descriptionOriginal: While millennials and Gen Zers often get lumped together as the “young group,” they are certainly not the same . (Although it is kind of hard to tell with all the Y2K fashion floating around.) But speaking as a millennial, we definitely have different approaches to life , many of which seem to come down to a sense of self-assurance. That goes for shopping, socializing, self-expression, and even going to the hair salon, apparently. Alexis Rex ( @rex.artistry ), hairstylist and owner of Rex Artistry Salon in Maryland, gave a brilliant (and hilarious) demonstration of some key personality differences between her millennial clients and her Gen Z clients in a now-viral TikTok video. Meet your millennial client, a nervous wreck First, Rex played her Millennial Customer. Millennial Customer gently knocks on the door and immediately expresses her gratitude. “Hey girl! So good to see you! So excited!” But at the same time, Millennial Customer wants in no way to be an inconvenience, so she immediately comes back with, “Where should I put my purse? It’s okay, I’m just going to shove it in my own personal space so it’s not in your way. At all.” Never one to demand attention, Millennial Customer wants a very subtle hair color change. Really, “it shouldn’t even look like I got my hair done.” Then after flooding the hairstylist with compliments, Millennial Customer (ever wanting to be a good student) will ask a bunch of follow-up questions about how to maintain the style. Gen Z enters the building, no apologies Then, Rex played her Gen Z Customer. Gen Z Customer bolts through the door with a “Hey queen!” like a hurricane (who has time to knock?!) and is ready to plop her stuff down anywhere. Unlike her millennial counterpart, Gen Z Customer is perfectly fine to take up space unapologetically and even show up with hair that “hasn’t been brushed in a month.” Gen Z Customer also knows exactly what she wants, and it’s anything but subtle. “I wanna do like in-your-face, bold contrast…I wanna look like a different f**king person. Let’s do it.” The confidence… it’s… palpable . Gen Z Customer has a different approach to complementing her hairstylist: “Oh my god! F**king Queen! You did that! God I love you.” No further questions. Gen Z Customer already knows her brand of hair care products, and it’s “Olaplex. All Olaplex.” The comments went full group therapy Rex’s post quickly racked up 8.6 million views , generating literally tens of thousands of comments about how spot-on her imitations were. Millennials in particular chimed in, many of whom couldn’t help but applaud its accuracy of depicting how millennials seem to constantly be apologizing for simply existing. “I’m a millennial and once I missed the armhole for a sec when putting the cape on. I was convinced I had ruined the appointment,” wrote one person. Another added, “I’m sorry for my hair. I’m sorry my hair takes so long. I’m sorry I had to move my head, omg I’m sorry. You offered me a drink? I will say yes. And then sorry.” Many were also quick to applaud how Gen Zers seemed to have no issues in this arena. “ Gen Z just fully owning the ability to take up space ,” one person commented. “As a millennial I love Gen Z so much. They’re so free to be themselves and so open,” wrote another. While there may be differences between generations , we can all learn something from one another . And we all enjoy getting our hair did. By the way, Rex didn’t leave out her Gen X or Boomer clients. She has plenty of videos of her imitating them, as well as some nifty style predictions on her TikTok, found here . items.descriptionOriginal: There are simple things we know to be true about happiness : Going for a walk in the sunshine just feels good. So does a hug, or hearing your favorite song. Petting a dog puts most of us in a better mood. And so does a little bit of intense exercise. Maybe not during, but definitely after, when we’re basking in the afterglow of our effort. The science behind life’s simple pleasures is where things start to get really interesting. Happiness isn’t just one feeling, it’s a collection of several different feelings, and many of them come from our brain’s internal pharmacy of “ feel good ” chemicals, or neurochemicals. They’re known as the four happy hormones: oxytocin, serotonin, dopamine, and endorphins. The big questions of existence like finding our purpose, doing work that matters, and finding love aside, it’s really the little things that send our brain happiness signals throughout the day. And these feelings are really easy to trigger intentionally, once you know how. Simple daily habits can trigger the chemicals your brain uses to make you feel good. Photo credit: Canva Oxytocin: love, bonding & connection Oxytocin is known as the “love hormone,” and is most famous for playing a big role during childbirth. No wonder it’s highly associated with deep feelings of love, connection, belonging, bonding, and more. In short, it feels incredible, and a burst of oxytocin can be an overwhelmingly positive and life-affirming feeling. But you don’t have to give birth or go on a romantic date to activate this neurochemical. Here are a few things you can do to release oxytocin each and every day. Some of them might surprise you: Any kind of physical human touch can do the trick. A long hug with someone you care about is ideal, but the touch doesn’t have to be associated with love, affection, or sex by any means. The professional, friendly touch from a massage or haircut can do wonders for your brain. Hair, especially, is inherently emotional for a lot of people, and in addition to the light human touch, a fresh look boosts self-esteem, mood, and more. In the absence of touch, prolonged eye contact can be just as powerful at helping your brain release oxytocin. If there aren’t any people you love around, try your dog: Veterinarian Dr. Julie Hunt at Embrace Pet Insurance tells Upworthy that a 2015 study found that when dogs and owners gaze at each other, both produce more oxytocin. You don’t necessarily need a willing partner to touch you or stare into your eyes, whether they have two legs or four. Dr. Clint Salo from The Grove Recovery tells Upworthy that giving someone, even a stranger, a genuine compliment can have a powerful and positive effect on us. “Giving a genuine compliment can increase oxytocin by creating a brief moment of social connection,” he says. Taking all of those positive feelings and writing them down is another technique that yields terrific results. As cheesy as it might feel, writing a line or two of gratitude in a journal may help you feel more connected. Chelsea Pottenger, author and founder of EQ Minds , suggests another method: “Write a letter to someone you love, even if you never send it. Just by writing it, it gives an oxytocin hit.” Finally, if all else fails, give yourself a hug. It’s both important and effective. Serotonin: positive mood & euphoria Serotonin is an absolutely crucial piece of “feeling happy.” Serotonin is closely tied to mood, and SSRIs, one of the main treatments for depression, work by boosting serotonin signaling in the brain. A 2022 review found no consistent evidence that low serotonin causes depression, but the chemical still plays a key role in our overall mood, demeanor, and wellbeing. It’s a natural mood stabilizer, helps regulate our sleep cycles, promotes learning and memory, and helps arousal and libido. There are a few simple and surprising ways you can get a serotonin boost during the day and feel better almost instantly: Even if you don’t have Seasonal Affective Disorder, almost everyone reports feeling a little cheerier on a bright sunny day versus a rainy one. It turns out, sunlight is absolutely crucial to our serotonin levels. Dr. Sam Zand, CEO and psychiatrist at Anywhere Clinic , tells Upworthy that a few minutes of sunshine first thing in the day does wonders: “Serotonin is highly affected by light and rhythm. Getting bright natural light during the first hour of the day will really help you maintain good moods.” Because serotonin plays such a crucial role in memory, accessing positive memories can put us in a much better mood. Lisa Chen, LMFT and founder of Lisa Chen & Associates Therapy , tells Upworthy that one of the most powerful links to memory is actually our sense of smell, and we can use that to our advantage: “Smell something tied to a happy memory, like cinnamon. Scent has a straight line to emotional memory centers and can quickly shift our moods.” Random acts of kindness make us feel great, and now we know why: It’s the serotonin. Pottenger tells Upworthy : “Do something for a stranger without expecting anything back. When you perform a random act of kindness with no strings attached, your brain releases serotonin.” Finally, here’s a little trick that makes good use of our anatomy. Research suggests the vagus nerve is key to triggering the release and transport of serotonin. Intentional breathwork and even light humming or singing can stimulate that nerve and give us a little extra boost. One thing that gets in the way of serotonin is stress, and its primary neurochemical, cortisol. Anything you can do to lower stress may improve your serotonin levels, like taking a few minutes for yoga, meditation, or just practicing better mindfulness. Dopamine: reward, pleasure & motivation We get a rush of dopamine in our brains whenever we feel pleasure or reward, whether it’s ultimately good or bad for us. Sex, sweets, drugs, gambling, flirting, achieving a goal. They all give us some form of pleasure or satisfaction, and they’re driven by this very specific (and feel-good) neurochemical. That makes dopamine a tricky one to navigate. Chasing it can be destructive, but luckily, there are plenty of natural and healthy ways to get the same pleasurable result: Achieving a goal, even a small one, gives us a dopamine boost. This can be as simple as checking something off your to-do list. Zand tells Upworthy that dopamine is “very responsive to ‘micro-completions,’ meaning you can get a little shot of dopamine by completing small tasks like sending a text or cleaning one area of the house.” Believe it or not, dopamine also responds positively to novelty. Changing even small things in our daily routine can give us a lovely little tingle of pleasure: Chen suggests things “like taking a new route or trying a new coffee flavor,” while Dr. Michael Valdez, Medical Director at Detox California , says it can be as simple as moving to another room to reset attention and focus. Dopamine loves a reward, but it also loves the anticipation of a reward. Kelly Whaling, Licensed Clinical Psychologist at Prosper Health , tells Upworthy “Anticipating a positive experience or even vividly picturing it, like planning a vacation, can trigger dopamine because your brain begins predicting a reward.” On a more physical level, a shock of cold water can trigger a substantial surge in dopamine. Research shows that an hour in 57-degree water can cause a 250% increase in dopamine. In the absence of a giant tub full of ice, a 30-second burst of cold water at the end of your shower is a lower-effort way to try the idea. Dopamine, however, can be a double-edged sword. We technically get a small hit of dopamine every time we log into social media and see something interesting, or when we get a notification on our phones. This constant drip can overstimulate our brain’s reward system, and some experts say it makes it harder to stay motivated to achieve goals and finish tasks. That’s why some people advocate for a “dopamine reset.” Eli Elad Cohen, Co-Founder and Co-CEO at MediTailor , recommends something called Non-Sleep Deep Rest. It’s a sort of guided meditation and breathwork practice that lowers stress and anxiety and helps us feel recharged when tired.” He points to a small 2002 study from Denmark that found about a 65% increase in dopamine release in one part of the brain during a session. It involved just eight experienced practitioners, so it’s an early finding. If that sounds too complicated, try going one hour without your phone in nature or focusing on a single task to get a similar effect. Endorphins: stress relief, pain relief & overall wellbeing In the famous words of Elle Woods from Legally Blonde , “Exercise gives you endorphins. Endorphins make you happy. Happy people just don’t shoot their husbands, they just don’t!” She’s not wrong. Harvard Health describes endorphins as the brain’s natural pain relievers that help relieve stress and promote an overall feeling of well-being. They most famously come from exercise (e.g. the “runner’s high”) but there are many other ways of activating them. Endorphins respond well to the arts. Listening to music or creating art of any kind is a great way to promote that feel-good sensation in your body. Bonus points if the song you listen to gives you the “chills.” Eating spicy foods, while sometimes challenging, can also work. “[It] activates the body’s natural pain-relief and pleasure systems,” and releases endorphins, similar to a good workout, says Kelly Whaling. Steven Sultanoff, Adjunct Professor of Psychology at Pepperdine University , suggests laughter. If you’re feeling down, try listening to some stand-up comedy or putting on an old favorite sitcom episode. “Laughter results in the secretion of endorphins. Humor also relaxes the brain by generating perspective and shifting negative thinking to realistic thinking,” he says. Here’s a tip you might recognize: Humming or singing quietly, stimulating the vagus nerve, can also produce endorphins. Fascinatingly, exercise doesn’t release endorphins simply to reward you for a job well done. It does so in response to physical exertion, pain, and stress. So the rule with endorphins is that sometimes, we have to feel a little bad before we can feel good. Dr. Michael Drzewiecki, Director of Clinical Neuroscience at The Neurologic Wellness Institute , puts it this way: “Doing hard things for short periods of time releases ‘feel bad’ chemicals called dynorphin, which leads to an upregulation of endorphin receptors. Essentially, to get a greater release of ‘feel good’ chemicals, it’s best to do something hard enough to trigger a short duration of ‘feel bad’ chemical release.” Take this as a sign to finally have that tough conversation, tackle that home project, or challenge yourself physically and mentally. Stacking the four for the best results The four “happy brain chemicals” don’t always work alone. Many times, they operate in tandem. There are many different dietary strategies and theories out there about how to optimize your brain health, but there does seem to be at least one “super food,” when it comes to feeling happy: Dark chocolate. Chocolate is associated with all four of these chemicals, though the evidence is still limited. But if you’re not a fan, don’t worry. Many of the tips and activities recommended by experts serve many purposes at once. Going for a walk in the sunshine with your dog can give you a rush of serotonin and oxytocin. Pairing breathwork and meditation before or after a workout can give you endorphins and serotonin. “Romantic time” with a partner can give you all four simultaneously. We have more control over how we feel than we might think. While petting a dog or having a nibble of dark chocolate can’t account for your overall satisfaction and contentment with life and existence, these little daily things can bring us substantial joy in the moment. When we stack them consistently, we’re bound to feel pretty damn happy most of the time. This article originally appeared in April It has been updated. The post The 4 brain chemicals that make you feel amazing, and simple ways you can trigger each one appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: Most self-help advice gets one major aspect wrong: the habits that actually change your life aren’t the dramatic ones. They’re not 5 a.m. cold plunges or 75-day fitness challenges . They’re much more subtle, and almost embarrassingly ordinary. But that’s the point. Done consistently, the small stuff shapes how you feel, how you show up to the world, and the person you become over time . YouTube user Ideas to Thrive understands this essential truth. In a video, “17 Boring Habits That Quietly Rebuilt My Life,” they detail 17 “embarrassingly easy habits that are too small to fail.” The ideas are simple: create bite-sized routines that fit seamlessly into your day, and build different versions of those systems for different days, whether good or chaotic. The goal is to stick with these practices, daily or weekly, even on turbulent days when nothing seems to go right. They write: “Traditional productivity advice assumes perfect conditions. This system assumes chaos is inevitable and builds protocols for bad days. You’re not trying to be perfect. You’re trying to be unbreakable.” Here are 14 deceptively simple habits worth trying, courtesy of Ideas to Thrive : Health and wellness Intensity, not length, is important here. Photo credit: Canva 1. Start with embarrassingly easy workouts Jump-starting a healthier lifestyle doesn’t require a gym membership. You don’t need a plan, a new playlist, or special gear. You just need a dedicated block during the day to move: a short walk, five squats while the coffee brews in the morning, or committing to taking the stairs instead of the elevator. If this all sounds too small, too trivial to matter, listen to this: Harvard Health reported on a study tracking nearly 72,000 adults that found just 15 minutes of vigorous activity per week was associated with a 17% lower risk of dying, and about 50 minutes per week with a 36% lower risk. The takeaway? Even short bursts of intense exercise can make a measurable difference. You don’t need an hour a day. Even a few minutes of effort can count. 2. Drink water before anything else Before your morning coffee, juice, or that special loose-leaf tea your father-in-law got you (thanks, Perry!), drink a glass of water. Then have another about 30 minutes before your first meal. Why? Your stomach has stretch-sensing nerves that help let your brain know when you’re full. In a small study published in Clinical Nutrition Research , 15 young adults who drank 300 milliliters of water before a meal ate less than when they drank none. It’s not magic, and it’s not proof of weight loss, but it’s a simple trick that costs nothing. 3. Put your phone in another room at night This one’s tricky. What about your morning alarm? (Buy one. It’s good to know the time without constantly checking your phone.) What about that nightly Sudoku game you have to do? (Try a book of puzzles, or the one printed in the newspaper.) Research increasingly suggests that smartphones in the bedroom can disrupt sleep. By removing your phone, you eliminate both the temptation to scroll and the device lighting up with notifications during the night. According to a 2023 survey by the American Academy of Sleep Medicine, 87% of U.S. adults regularly sleep with their phones in the bedroom, despite evidence linking the habit to poorer sleep. Some studies have found that limiting bedtime phone use can improve sleep quality and mood. Luckily, the fix isn’t a fancy gadget. It’s as simple as leaving your phone on the kitchen counter. 4. While you’re at it, write down tomorrow’s one task before bed Before you sleep, jot down the single most important thing you need to do the next day. That’s it: one thing. Psychologists call our tendency to dwell on unfinished tasks the Zeigarnik effect, after Soviet psychologist Bluma Zeigarnik, who studied it in 1927. It suggests that unfinished tasks stay active in our minds, using up mental energy and potentially disrupting sleep. Writing down a plan to complete them can help ease these restless thoughts, reassuring your brain that it’s okay to let go because a clear plan is in place. Further research shows that having a written plan boosts productivity, as the act of planning helps lighten your mental load. The takeaway? Your brain can’t file away a task until it trusts there’s a plan. Give it one sentence tonight. 5. Take a 10-minute walk after lunch That 2 p.m. slump? It’s not just because of the family-style Jersey Mike’s hoagie you wolfed down ( no judgment , though it didn’t help). Afternoon sleepiness is real, but a short walk can actually help tremendously. Post-meal walking is one of the most well-studied micro-habits in metabolic health . A small New Zealand study of adults with type 2 diabetes found that a 10-minute walk after each main meal lowered blood sugar more effectively than a single 30-minute walk taken at another time of day. UCLA Health notes that even a five-minute walk after eating can have a measurable effect on blood sugar. That’s the entire prescription: 10 minutes around the block. How much simpler can it get? Productivity and mindset What are you grateful for? Photo credit: Canva 6. Write three sentences to yourself before bed Here’s a gentle, minimal journaling practice: Write three sentences to yourself in a notebook before bed. Answer the following: What are you thinking about? What are you grateful for? What do you want to release before resting? Bedtime worry and rumination about incomplete tasks aren’t trivial; they’re significant contributors to difficulty falling asleep. A brief journaling session before bed acts as a form of cognitive off-loading, moving those swirling thoughts from active working memory onto the page and signaling to the brain that they’ve been “handled.” A 2018 Baylor University study of 57 young adults in the Journal of Experimental Psychology: General found that those who wrote a to-do list before bed fell asleep faster than those who wrote about tasks they had already finished. Some research suggests gratitude journaling before bed may help too. Your brain wasn’t designed to hold everything. Three sentences are enough to start letting go. 7. Track your habits with color Find a visual tracker that works for you, whether on paper or in a digital app, and assign yourself colors: Green for done Yellow for partially complete Red for skipped Yes, it may sound like an elementary school exercise (what’s next, a pizza party for finishing your books?), but there’s real science behind it. Research on digital behavior change tools suggests that visual feedback, such as a green bar for steps completed and a red line for the daily target, can boost motivation. Visual feedback can be powerful. Soon, you’ll start noticing patterns you didn’t even realize were there. 8. Set aside 20 minutes on Sunday for a quick self-review No one’s under fire; this isn’t a productivity audit. You are not in trouble. But a little self-reflection never hurt, did it? Without deliberate reflection, it’s easy to stay on autopilot. Reviews create the feedback loop necessary for intentional progress. During these sessions, ask yourself: What went well this week? What didn’t? What does next week look like? Should I adjust my self-improvement expectations? Reviewing the week allows you to “bank” wins, process setbacks, and make small, purposeful improvements (a strategy shown to reduce burnout). David Allen, the productivity consultant and author of Getting Things Done, notes that the weekly review “will sharpen your intuitive focus on your important projects as you deal with the flood of new input and potential distractions coming at you the rest of the week.” By spending 20 minutes looking back each week, you can avoid going 20 weeks in the wrong direction. 9. Close all your browser tabs at the end of the day Every open tab is an unfinished thought. Research from Princeton University and the University of California, Los Angeles suggests that physical clutter competes for the brain’s attention and is linked to higher stress. Digital clutter likely works the same way. Closing your tabs at the same time each day creates a shutdown ritual that helps separate work from rest, a clear boundary that prevents lingering anxiety during off-hours. This distinction is especially important for those who work from home. Productivity experts also note that fewer digital distractions means fewer choices and less noise, which in turn reduces decision fatigue and increases the likelihood that tasks get done. Your browser is not a filing cabinet. Close those tabs. Start fresh tomorrow. 10. Read 10 pages per day That’s it: 10 pages. That’s about 15 minutes of active reading. Do that every day, and you’ll finish between 12 and 18 books a year (unless you’re working your way through the Dune series. Those books are seriously hefty). It’s good for you, too: a widely cited 2009 study led by a University of Sussex neuropsychologist reported that just six minutes of reading can reduce stress levels by up to 68%. Ten pages a day is more than just a light reading habit; it’s an insurance policy for your brain’s health. Social and emotional life Saying “no” is a deliberate practice. Photo credit: Canva 11. Say no to one thing per week Despite the wisdom in Year of Yes by Shonda Rhimes, treating “no” as a weekly maintenance habit isn’t an act of selfishness; it’s an act of self-preservation. Chronic people-pleasing drains the same mental and emotional resources that support creativity, focus, and recovery. Research consistently shows that excessive stress, the kind caused by overcommitting, is a major trigger for depression, anxiety disorders, and burnout. Therapist Keisha Moore writes in Psychology Today that saying no “can create more mental health stability by helping with self-care and build your self-esteem and confidence by setting boundaries.” This is a deliberate practice. Decline at least one request, invitation, or obligation each week that doesn’t align with your priorities. When you set limits on what drains you, you create space for restorative activities . 12. Send one thoughtful message a week Every week, send one intentional message to someone in your life: a text, email, or note that’s personal, specific, and sincere. Social connection is one of the strongest predictors of health and longevity. A landmark meta-analysis by Brigham Young University researcher Julianne Holt-Lunstad found that a lack of social relationships was equivalent to smoking up to 15 cigarettes a day and more harmful than obesity or physical inactivity. A study published in Communication Research , involving 900 participants across five university campuses, found that even a single intentional outreach to a friend or loved one on any given day can significantly improve well-being, reduce stress, and enhance connection. Importantly, the research showed that no particular type of message, whether catching up, showing care, joking, or giving a compliment, was more effective than another. The key factor was the act of reaching out with intention. Home and money Don’t rely on willpower alone for this one. Photo credit: Canva 13. Automate your savings Don’t rely on willpower alone for this one. Set up an automatic transfer from every paycheck into savings, even if it’s a small percentage. Richard Thaler and Shlomo Benartzi’s groundbreaking research found that automated savings programs significantly increase how much people save over time. The reason? It’s far easier to commit to saving money in the future than to cut current spending. Automation removes the friction of decision-making . It turns out the best savings plan is the one that runs without you having to make a single decision. 14. Do a two-minute tidy every night Dishes in the sink. Clothes on the chair. Scattered envelopes on the dining room table. Spend two minutes before bed restoring basic order to your space: reset surfaces, return items to their places, and clear clutter. Research conducted by UCLA , involving 32 dual-income families, found that individuals who described their homes as cluttered or full of unfinished projects showed elevated cortisol patterns linked to chronic stress, especially among women. Allen’s Getting Things Done methodology helps explain why the two-minute rule works so well. As he explains , any task that can be completed in under two minutes should be done immediately rather than delayed, preventing small messes from building into overwhelming chaos. One small step at a time None of these habits will change your life overnight. You won’t wake up with a different bank account. Your apartment won’t magically become more organized; you’ll probably still lose focus around 3:33 p.m. each day. But that’s not really how change works, is it? It happens in the small, consistent moments that may not look impressive on paper but add up to real momentum. You don’t need to overhaul your entire life. Ideas to Thrive recommends starting with a handful of habits, then slowly adding more. Pick a few and see where they take you. This article originally appeared in April It has been updated. The post 14 boring habits that can quietly rebuild your life, according to science appeared first on Upworthy .

Αναγνωρίζουν τα πρόσωπα των ανθρώπων που τους αρέσουν ή δεν τους αρέσουν, έχουν την ικανότητα να σας…
items.descriptionOriginal: When it comes to keeping birds as pets, people usually think about parrots or canaries. Nobody ever considers having a crow . But research has shown that crows are incredibly clever and curious, and a 2020 study found they are capable of a basic form of consciousness. They recognize the faces of people they like or don’t like, have the ability to use tools, and some can even mimic human speech. Looking to experience the magic of crows yourself? A YouTube user named Alexandra from Germany made a video on how you can befriend the crows in your neighborhood in four easy steps. All it takes is “some food and some patience.” Years ago, Alexandra made friends with a crow named Krari. Krari and friends visit Alexandra regularly and are considered part of the family. They also bring their “little ones” to Alexandra’s house to chill. “They come here to get food, to play, or just hang out with me and relax,” Alexandra says in an introductory video on her YouTube page. How to make friends with a crow in four steps 1. Find a pair of crows Crows tend to live in areas populated by humans, so chances are there are crows in your neighborhood. The best place to start is to find a pair with a fixed territory that you see on a regular basis. That way, you’re cultivating a relationship with the same animal day after day, and you can “slowly get to know each other.” 2. Offer food Crows will eat a wide range of foods, from insects to meat. They also enjoy nuts, worms, and vegetables, but avoid bread, chocolate, and anything salted or spiced. If you offer the food in the same place at the same time of day, you’ll establish a routine. Then, the crow may come by regularly to see if you have anything tasty to eat. 3. Be mindful When interacting with the crow, make sure they aren’t anxious or displaying signs that they are prepared to fly away at any moment. Approach the birds with an open, indirect gaze so as not to cause alarm. Sit quietly while you wait for the bird to approach and avoid quick movements. 4. Let the birds come to you This requires patience. The crow will be shy at first, but they know you better than you think. They will remember your face and your kindness. Give them a chance to observe you and earn your trust. One important reminder before you start At the end of the video, Alexandra reminds everyone that while we should make friends with crows, they are supposed to live free in the skies and not be stuck in a cage. “I hope this helps you build a relationship with these fascinating birds,” Alexandra concludes her video. “They are loyal friends and have brought much joy into my life. Please let birds have their freedom. They do not belong in homes or other forms of captivity. Thank you.” If you succeeded in befriending a feathered genius, tell your new crow friend we say hi! This article originally appeared five years ago. It has been updated. The post Crows are incredibly smart. Here’s how to make friends with one in four easy steps. appeared first on Upworthy .

items.descriptionOriginal: There are several stories written about music taming the savage beast, but this is no fairy tale . A video shows a small pride of lions in an enclosure listening to the acoustic guitar and soothing singing of a French singer-songwriter covering Guns N’ Roses’ “November Rain.” One would think that the animals would be annoyed by the music or simply ignore it. Instead, something heartwarming happened. One by one, the lions approached the musician known as Plumes as he performed. They calmly lay down and started yawn-singing to the tunes while nuzzling one another, with two lions cuddling less than a yard from where Plumes sat and played on the other side of the fence. The lions were relaxing and enjoying the concert, and some even seemed ready for a nap, showing off the gentler side of the predatory wild cats. View this post on Instagram People remarked upon the lions’ reaction to Plumes’ tunes: “Wow! That is truly an incredible interaction with them. They really enjoyed your singing to them.” “Omg, the way they cuddle.” “What a beautiful interaction to witness.” “Music is the universal language!” “That was so magical! Music speaks to the soul. Human, animal, all relate to the feelings music evokes.” This wasn’t his first animal concert This isn’t the only time Plumes has performed for an animal audience. In fact, his social media and YouTube channel show videos of multiple concerts for humans and creatures alike. He has played guitar and sung for lions, tigers and bears, along with many other animals at wildlife sanctuaries and zoos. It all started with some cows While Plumes performs his music for a wide variety of animals today, he started at home, playing for a herd of cows in the French countryside while living with his grandmother. “I read somewhere that cows like music, that it’s soothing to them,” Plumes shared with AMFM Magazine . “They were super receptive. They gathered around, some even rubbed against me. It was magical.” Since then, Plumes had been taking the opportunity to warm up his vocal cords and provide various animals a free mini-concert throughout his tours and travels, recording video of their reactions to his music. “Animals inspire me to be kinder, more patient,” he added. “They remind us to reconnect with nature. Maybe we’ve lost touch with nature, and these videos help people feel that connection again.” The science backs this up too Understandably, most people believe music and music appreciation are uniquely human traits, but there are studies suggesting that music isn’t exclusively for Homo sapiens’ enjoyment. Some studies show different species reacting positively to music in different ways. Chimpanzees have been observed swaying to classical music, dogs in rehoming centers showed calmer behavior when classical music was played, and a sea lion named Ronan was able to bob her head in time with a beat, just to name a few. Some veterinarians also suggest creating a music playlist for your dog to play when you leave the house to help ease separation anxiety. It’s interesting to see how music impacts different animals in different ways, especially if music helps them. Over time, who knows how much music will bring man and animal closer together. If a lion can enjoy Guns N’ Roses, the possibilities are nearly endless. This article originally appeared last year. It has been updated. The post Three lions have the most beautiful reaction to a man singing a Guns N’ Roses song to them appeared first on Upworthy .

items.title: «Οι προηγμένες χειρουργικές τεχνολογίες δεν πρέπει να περιορίζονται σε πόλεις μετρό»: Πώς αυτοί οι ιδρυτές κατασκεύασαν ένα εγχώριο χειρουργικό GPS
